events.text: {npc} has started leaving the house before dawn and coming back with ink on {his} hands and nothing to say. Tonight you find a half-written letter to a sect you have never heard {him} mention.

mem.note: asked instead of accusing

effects.log: {He} is writing to the sect that raised {him}, which {he} left without permission and which has found {him} again. {He} has been afraid to tell you for a year.

choices.text: Read the rest of the letter

mem.note: read my letters

effects.log: The letter is a refusal. The sect wants {him} back. {He} finds you reading it, and the house is cold for a season.

events.text: The sect's envoy comes for {npc} in daylight: {he} swore an oath, and oaths are not undone by marriage. {He} looks at you, not at the envoy.

mem.note: stood between me and my sect

ok.log: The envoy leaves without {him}. The sect sends a letter: the oath is released, in return for a favour they will name later.

mem.note: bled for me at our own gate

fail.log: The envoy is the stronger, and you are on the ground when {npc} steps over you and agrees to settle the oath properly. {He} goes for a year, and comes back thinner, free, and {his} own.

mem.note: let me choose my own oath

effects.log: {He} goes with the envoy for a year to settle the oath, and comes back thinner, free, and {his} own.

events.text: {npc} falls ill in the autumn with a wasting sickness the physicians cannot name. The best of them says a year, perhaps two, and that a certain snow lotus in the far mountains might be more.

mem.note: crossed the mountains for my life

ok.log: Four months. You come back frostbitten with the lotus wrapped in your shirt. {He} lives, and tells the story better than you do.

fail.deathCause: the mountains, for a snow lotus
fail.log: The cold takes everything you have. You turn back below the pass with frostbite and no lotus, and spend the year the physicians promised at the bedside.

choices.text: Buy every year the physicians can give

mem.note: spent everything to keep me

effects.log: Two years, then three, then the sickness simply stops, as such things sometimes do. The house is poor and full of {his} laughter.

mem.note: stayed by my bed through the bad nights

effects.log: You learn the physicians' broths and sit up through the bad nights. It is a long, poor year, then a second. Slowly, the way such things sometimes go, the sickness loosens its hold. {He} lives.

events.text: An old age. {npc} finds the letter from the first year, the half-written one, in a chest, and reads it aloud to you with {his} glasses on, laughing at {his} own handwriting.

mem.note: laughed with me at the end

effects.log: You spend the evening reading old letters. It is the best one of the year, and there have been many good ones.

mem.note: asked the question

effects.log: {He} thinks about it honestly, which is why you married {him}, and says no. Then {he} says: once, for an afternoon.

events.text: {npc} is small and has been copying your forms from the doorway for a month, badly and in secret. Today {he} asks if {he} may learn.

choices.text: Teach {him}, properly, from the first stance

mem.note: taught me the first stance

effects.log: An hour every dawn. {He} is not gifted, and does not care, and that is the gift.

choices.text: Not yet. Let {him} be a child

effects.log: {He} keeps copying from the doorway. At ten {he} shows you a form you never taught, learned entirely from watching.

events.text: {npc} comes home from the village school with a split lip and a story: the magistrate's son said your name in the wrong tone, and {he} answered it.

choices.text: Tell {him} fighting over a name is foolish

mem.note: told me names are not worth blood

effects.log: {He} nods and does not believe you, which is fair, because you did not believe your own parent either.

choices.text: Teach {him} to answer it better next time

mem.note: took my side

effects.log: Three months of footwork. The magistrate's son learns a new tone.

events.text: {npc} is nearly grown and wants to leave for a sect that is not yours, three provinces away, because, {he} says, {he} will never be more than your child here.

choices.text: Let {him} go, with a letter and a purse

mem.note: let me go my own way

effects.log: {He} writes twice a year. The sect makes {him} an inner disciple in three. {His} letters stop calling you by your title.

mem.note: kept me home

effects.log: Two sullen years. Then {he} leaves anyway, the day {he} can, without the letter or the purse.

events.text: A letter from {npc}: {he} has passed a gate that took you years to cross, and {he} wants to know, honestly, whether you are proud or jealous.

mem.note: said they were proud of me

effects.log: {His} reply is one line long and you keep it in your sleeve for a year.

mem.note: told me the truth about pride

effects.log: {He} laughs, in the letter, and says that is the first time you have talked to {him} as a martial artist rather than a child.

events.text: {npc} comes home grey at the temples, with a child of {his} own who copies your forms from the doorway, badly and in secret.

choices.text: Teach the grandchild the first stance

mem.note: taught my child as they taught me

effects.log: An hour every dawn. {npc} watches from the doorway, and says nothing, and does not need to.

mem.note: let me be the teacher

effects.log: {He} teaches it exactly as you did, including the mistake you made. You decide not to mention it.

events.text: {npc}'s hands have started to shake. She hides it by keeping them busy, and by sending you to market so you will not see her try to thread a needle.

mem.note: brought the physician I would not ask for

effects.log: The physician says years, not months, if she rests. She does not rest. She has years anyway.

choices.text: Thread the needles and say nothing

mem.note: threaded my needles

effects.log: You thread them every evening for a decade. Neither of you ever says why.

events.text: {npc}, who has never asked you for anything, asks you to come home for a season: the roof, the field, the debt he has not mentioned for six years.

mem.note: came home when I asked

effects.log: You mend the roof and pay the debt and he pretends the money was his. It is the last season you spend under his roof.

choices.text: Write that you cannot come this year

mem.note: wrote instead of coming

effects.log: He writes back that he understands, in a hand shakier than you remember. The roof is patched by a neighbour. He never asks again.

events.text: The house you came from is being cleared out. In the rafters, where the family kept things, there is a box with your baby teeth, every letter you sent, and a manual nobody in the family could read.

effects.log: A breathing method, old and plain, in your great-grandmother's hand. The family was never ordinary. It had simply forgotten.

choices.text: Keep the box closed and the house standing

effects.log: You pay a neighbour to keep the roof whole. Every few years you sit in the empty kitchen for an hour.
